low_resolution_finding.evidence: Under the SHARED adaptive flattener the same glyphs measure 0.9949-0.9994 at cap 1024, where the earlier mixed-flattener comparison measured 0.942-0.996 at 61-73 px. The deficit was flattening and rasterisation, not conversion damage.

vector_gate.defect: nearest_dists() measures point-to-VERTEX distance between two independently sampled polylines. Adaptive flattening places vertices at different arc positions on the two representations, so a vertex can sit several units from the nearest opposing VERTEX while lying essentially on the opposing SEGMENT. The gate wants point-to-SEGMENT (Hausdorff to the curve), which I did not implement.
vector_gate.corroboration: Enclosed-area difference is 0.0004-0.1444 percent and every raster IoU is at or above 0.995 — both impossible if the outlines really deviated by 4-6 font units.

repeated_error_note: This is the second time in this workstream that a distance metric of mine produced a false negative — first SAME_ROW versus LOCAL_NORMAL in VQ-1, now point-to-vertex versus point-to-segment here. The pattern is measuring against sampled points instead of against the curve.
why_no_inspections: Section 11 gates inspection behind full deterministic certification. The vector gate is unresolved, so the two inspections were correctly not run.
next_step: Replace nearest-vertex with point-to-segment distance, re-run the vector gate, then fixtures, inspections and package. No geometry change is expected or authorised.
